driver.composition: The Controller generates an Authority signing keypair and per-Task authorized Online client keypairs. Each private key is injected only after host-process-guard.mjs has set the selected process security descriptor to a null DACL and a same-SID OpenProcess(PROCESS_VM_READ/WRITE_DAC) sibling probe has failed. Secrets then travel only over the parent's stdin pipe, never environment files or command arguments. Authority and client public keys are Owner/FSW-bound by exact Task. Every request is RSA-SHA256 signed over canonical bytes of the complete protocol/version, recipient, request ID, operation, full value, CAS condition/expected revision and lease/capability identity; every response covers the complete result, revision and high-water identity. Offline creates and owns the canonical parent, empty SQLite registry and signed anchor and serves only the explicit bootstrap operations below. Production maintains an authorized-client registry: #370, future #284 and synthetic disjoint test Tasks use distinct per-Task keys with no shared private key, while unbound sibling keys remain denied. Temporary bytes are used once for #370 and retained only as read-only historical evidence; durable Authority/client behavior is implemented in host-resource-fence.mjs with tests in host-resource-fence.test.mjs and consumed by single-writer.mjs/task-claim-github-publisher.mjs, never by silently retaining temporary code as production.
driver.credentialBoundary: Each selected process starts without secrets, applies a null process DACL and proves a same-SID sibling cannot open it for VM read or WRITE_DAC before receiving secrets through stdin. Only then does CodexSandboxOnline receive the GitHub token, real Octokit and its per-Task client private key, or CodexSandboxOffline receive the Authority private key. Public keys are Owner/FSW-bound by exact Task. Complete canonical request bytes are client-signed and complete result/revision/high-water bytes are Authority-signed. Ordinary Owner and Online have no protected-object write/WRITE_DAC/delete-child. Request files are add-only for Online and unreadable by other Online processes; production nonces encrypt to the authorized per-Task client public key. Same-SID siblings lack process handles and all relevant private keys, so key substitution, replay, forged response, process-memory access or file tamper cannot produce an accepted Host Claim.

The earlier no-live-Claim sentence is enforced for all fake-transport tests and does not authorize any #284 effect.

physicalDesign.authority: ONE_SHARED_SQLITE_CAS_FENCE_REGISTRY_DOCUMENT consulted by every current-source T06d/Native-C privileged Claim writer. The selected Host composition alone receives the registry mutation port and GitHub write transport; B/K/UI/Agent/request callers receive neither.
physicalDesign.productionComposition: A long-lived one-shot-per-operation CodexSandboxOffline Authority owns all registry and anchor mutation. CodexSandboxOnline transport/controller processes open only read facades and submit signed-protocol requests to that Authority. Native C rejects an absent/mismatched fence, the controller cannot publish without acquisition, and all repository callers including host-admission-source.test.mjs are migrated. The Offline-created protected objects grant no write/WRITE_DAC/delete-child to the ordinary Owner or Online SID; historical byte copies cannot open them for mutation and are never production entry points.
physicalDesign.credentialAndTransportBoundary: Selected processes apply a null process DACL and pass same-SID OpenProcess/handle negatives before receiving secrets through stdin. Only then does the selected Online process receive the GitHub token, real Octokit and its per-Task client private key, or the selected Offline Authority receive its private key. The authorized-client registry binds a distinct public key to each exact Task (#370, future #284 and synthetic test Tasks), enabling independently authorized concurrent contenders without shared private keys. Complete canonical request bytes (value, condition, expected revision, lease identity, recipient, operation and request ID) are client-signed; complete result/revision/high-water bytes are Authority-signed. Same-SID siblings lack process handles and all relevant private keys and cannot produce a valid accepted Claim; direct file tamper causes signed high-water verification to fail.
physicalDesign.atomicity: The complete active-lease registry is one CAS document with a Host-configured registryId, mutated only by Offline Authority. Acquisition re-reads and validates the whole document, compares all exclusive resources and atomically adds one lease using mustBeAbsent for first initialization or mustMatchRevision thereafter. Claim/FSW store facades forward put conditions plus the current lease nonce; Authority validates key/phase/resource binding before executing them. At most 16 CAS retries are allowed; exhaustion returns HOST_RESOURCE_FENCE_CONTENTION_EXHAUSTED with zero Claim effect.
physicalDesign.continuousPossession: The random owner nonce is decrypted and retained only in the authorized per-Task Online process; CAS stores its SHA256 only. Every privileged stage sends canonical bytes covering protocol/version, recipient, fresh request ID, operation, expected identity, complete value and CAS condition/expected revision, signed by that Task's authorized client. Offline Authority re-reads registry/anchor, validates the authorized-client registry entry, registryId, fenceId, stable fenceRevision, nonce hash and exact binding, then signs the complete result/revision/high-water response. Leases never expire and no other writer can release without the nonce. The controller never releases during an in-flight effect, so protocol-compliant competitors cannot remove/reacquire between the final check and POST. Wrong-nonce release, overlapping acquisition, client-key substitution, request-value/condition tamper, replay, forged response or fabricated replacement denies.
physicalDesign.stableIdentity: fenceId and fenceRevision are assigned once at acquisition and never change when unrelated leases update the containing CAS row. The CAS row revision is a separate optimistic-concurrency value and is never serialized as the stable fenceRevision. fenceRevision equals the monotonically increasing registry generation at acquisition.
physicalDesign.lifetime: Definite pre-effect denial may release the still-owned lease. Successful publication and ambiguous/pending states retain it for Task ownership. Restarted processes do not receive the old nonce and cannot assert, release or reacquire the same resource set; recovery remains blocked pending native/CAS reconciliation. No automatic takeover or reset.
physicalDesign.registryRecreation: A null registry document is accepted only for the explicitly configured first initialization. Later null, changed registryId, generation regression, malformed document or deleted/recreated state is UNKNOWN and denies, never an empty-registry permit. The registry document itself is never deleted.
physicalDesign.rollbackAnchor: An independent append-only hash-and-signature chain anchor lives outside SQLite in the Offline-owned canonical parent and is writable only by Offline Authority. After every lease/Claim/FSW CAS, Authority computes the complete store snapshot (all keys, revisions and values), appends and fsyncs {registryId, generation, snapshotSha256, previousAnchorHash, writerSid} plus its RSA-SHA256 signature before any signed success or external effect. The expected current head is held in Authority process memory and checked before every operation; an Offline sibling cannot construct a new signed chain, and an unsigned/replayed/substituted chain fails. Authority restart never auto-recovers: with no in-memory expected head it refuses all operations and requires a separately reviewed Owner reconciliation, so restarted replay cannot grant access. Startup and every mutation also revalidate signatures, the complete chain and current generation/snapshot hash. CAS-success/anchor-failure, same-ID rollback, anchor-only truncation/replacement, generation regression or non-anchor mutation denies.
physicalDesign.publisherFence: Native C asserts the matching held lease immediately before and after each external POST. Omitting the port or using a mismatched/stale/lost lease prevents the POST or preserves pending evidence without retry. Fault injection at the transport boundary verifies the post-check/no-release invariant and uncertain-effect handling.
physicalDesign.resourceCompatibility: The PR #371 readHeldFence implementation derives compatibility from current durable foreign leases and their exact frozen resource objects, never from caller booleans or projected Claim fields. A foreign active Claim without a matching valid lease is incompatible. Snapshot drift retries only by re-running complete admission while still holding the lease; it never weakens conflict checks.

canonicalResourceContract.bytes: UTF-8 JSON.stringify of a recursive canonical value: plain object keys sorted by code unit; arrays retain semantic order except exclusive resource strings, which are sorted by code unit; undefined/functions/symbols/non-finite numbers/non-plain objects are rejected.
canonicalResourceContract.digest: frozenResourceSetSha256 = SHA256(canonicalBytes({schema, repository, issueRef, protectedClaimKey, generation, sourceSha, dispatchId, taskPackRef, taskPackBlobSha, reviewRef, ownerApprovalRef, writeSetSha256, exclusiveResources})). Recomputing the object must reproduce the port digest.
canonicalResourceContract.bindingVersusConflict: repository/issue/source/dispatch/Pack/review/Owner/write-set digest fields bind identity. Only normalized exclusiveResources participate in conflict comparison; metadata equality is still mandatory for possession.
canonicalResourceContract.file: Git repo-relative UTF-8 paths only: forward slashes, no empty/dot/dot-dot/backslash/drive/absolute/trailing-slash/NUL. Original Git spelling remains binding metadata. Conflict comparison uses the selected filesystem semantics: on the required Windows Host, paths are case-folded before exact/path-segment-ancestor comparison, so two Git paths differing only by case conflict and can never be declared disjoint; on case-sensitive Hosts the original case-sensitive comparison applies. Alias or unknown case/filesystem behavior denies.
canonicalResourceContract.cas: Exact validated CAS key string; only exact equality conflicts.
canonicalResourceContract.githubIssueComment: Canonical repository plus numeric Issue; the same Issue comment destination conflicts, different Issues are disjoint.
canonicalResourceContract.gitRef: Validated full refs/* name using code-unit comparison; exact or path-component ancestor ref conflicts.
canonicalResourceContract.gitWorktree: Only if a future Pack admits Agent effects: OS-canonical absolute realpath with Windows case folding, trailing separators removed and path-segment ancestor comparison. Alias, symlink, UNC/drive and ancestor negatives are mandatory before use.
canonicalResourceContract.unknown: Unknown resource types, duplicate/non-normalized resources or ambiguous path identity deny.
